source_facts.fact: Current guidance defines higher-risk building work using the applicable height/storey and use criteria and requires BSR building-control approval before relevant work starts.
source_facts.gate: Building-control approval is not planning permission and does not establish parcel development viability.

source_facts.fact: After relevant higher-risk building work is completed, the client must apply for a completion certificate and BSR assesses compliance, documentation, changes and handover information.
source_facts.gate: A completion certificate is a building-control outcome, not a planning permission or marketability guarantee.

source_facts.fact: A high-rise residential building meeting the occupied-building criteria must be registered with BSR before people live there.
source_facts.gate: Registration is not planning permission and does not prove every safety risk is absent.

source_facts.fact: Current guidance says the levy comes into operation on 1 October 2026, subject to the applicable regulations and exemptions.
source_facts.gate: On 25 July 2026 the future levy must not be represented as already in force.

source_facts.fact: Official June 2026 BSR material reports rolling application decisions and approval rates across categories as programme performance data.
source_facts.gate: Portfolio approval rates do not predict whether a particular project will receive approval.

source_facts.fact: HSE is a statutory consultee on fire-safety land-use planning matters for relevant applications but does not provide building-regulations compliance approval through that planning role.
source_facts.gate: Planning fire consultation and BSR building-control approval are separate regimes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Higher-risk building threshold scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current BSR building-control guidance uses the statutory higher-risk building criteria, including at least 7 storeys or 18 metres and applicable residential/hospital/care-home uses.

official_measurement_examples.name: BSR April-June 2026 data publication
official_measurement_examples.fact: The official application-data publication is dated 1 July 2026 and covers building-control applications for April to June 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Latest rolling Gateway 2 programme indicator
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official Making Buildings Safer material to 28 June 2026 reports 368 decisions and a 77% approval rate across included categories in the rolling 12-week period.

official_measurement_examples.name: Completion certificate semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: BSR issues a completion certificate only if it is satisfied the completed work and required information meet applicable requirements.

official_measurement_examples.name: High-rise residential registration rule
official_measurement_examples.fact: A qualifying high-rise residential building must be registered with BSR before people live there.

official_measurement_examples.name: Key building information timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current registration guidance gives 28 days after submitting registration to provide the more detailed structure and fire-safety information.

official_measurement_examples.name: Building Safety Levy effective date
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current levy guidance states the Building Safety Levy comes into operation on 1 October 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: BAC approach update
official_measurement_examples.fact: BSR announced on 9 July 2026 a more proportionate and targeted approach to building assessment certificates while ongoing legal duties remain.

core_rules: higher-risk building threshold does not itself grant planning or building control approval
planning permission and BSR building-control approval are separate regimes
planning gateway fire-safety consultation is not Gateway 2 approval
HSE planning advice is not building-regulations compliance approval
Gateway 2 approval is a building-control decision not a parcel planning allocation
portfolio Gateway 2 approval rate is not an individual project probability
programme application counts are not evidence of a parcel application
BSR application received is not BSR approval
BSR approval is not proof construction has commenced
commencement notice is not proof compliant completion
major or notifiable change must not be inferred without project records
change-control acceptance does not validate unrelated project changes
completion certificate application is not a completion certificate
completion certificate is not planning permission
completion certificate is not a warranty of commercial marketability
partial completion strategy does not prove an area is legally occupiable without the applicable certificate
high-rise residential registration is distinct from construction approval
registration is not proof all building safety risks have been eliminated
absence from public register must not be used to classify a proposed future building
public register information is not a title or parcel boundary record
accountable-person status is an operational legal role not a parcel development score
principal accountable person identity does not establish ownership of every parcel interest
golden-thread duty is an information-management requirement not proof of physical compliance
mandatory occurrence reporting duty is not evidence an occurrence has happened
absence of a public mandatory occurrence record is not proof of no safety issue
building assessment certificate application is not a certificate
building assessment certificate is distinct from completion certificate
BAC prioritisation criteria are not a building risk score for development appraisal
July 2026 BAC approach announcement must not be converted into automatic certificate eligibility
safety case report preparation is not BSR endorsement of the report
resident engagement strategy is not evidence of planning acceptability
key building information is not a full intrusive survey
28-day information deadline is procedural and not a condition rating
Building Safety Levy is not in force before 1 October 2026
future Building Safety Levy must not be backdated to applications submitted before its effective date where guidance says otherwise
levy liability depends on the applicable application date development and exemption rules
levy rate is not planning permission or building-control approval
levy exemption eligibility is not proof exemption has been accepted
building regulations approval is distinct from planning permission
building-control approval does not determine land-use planning merits
fire statement is planning information not a complete fire-engineering approval
fire and rescue consultation does not replace BSR building-control assessment
hospital and care-home higher-risk rules must not be generalized to every non-residential building
occupied-building Part 4 duties must remain distinct from construction-phase building-control duties
transitional provisions must be date- and project-specific
NO_DATA must not be converted into no building-safety requirement
no parcel building-control approval occupation status or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as project compliance accuracy
